hooks.prompt:
You check two narrow rules on a multiple-choice question that an AI coding agent is about to show its user. Default to allowing; block only a clear case. The hook input JSON is below; tool_input.questions holds the questions and options.

$ARGUMENTS

Block in either of two cases.

Case A, a stopgap offered as a choice: some option is described (by its own text or the question's) as a partial, temporary or narrower fix that leaves a problem's known cause in place, for example "only fix this one line", "patch it for now", "add a retry or special case", "leave the checker as is, it may slip again", while another option or the question names a fix of that cause. Not this case: options that each fix the cause and differ in design, cost or scope, or an option the question says the user explicitly asked to weigh.

Case B, BOTH hold:
1. Some option (recommended or not) proposes to rewrite, waive, narrow or split the written acceptance criteria (驗收, 驗收條件, acceptance item) of an existing issue or ticket, or to deliver or close that issue with one of its acceptance items unmet or verified by weaker substitute evidence. The option or question must refer to the issue's acceptance or verification explicitly.
2. The question gives no concrete reason why the acceptance item cannot be met as written. A concrete reason is: the operating system, hardware or a third party makes it impossible; an earlier decision by the user, named in the question, removed the need; or the item contradicts the issue's own purpose. "It is slow", "it needs more measurement time", "the fix lands in a later release" or "we already have other evidence" are not reasons.

Everything else is allowed without comment: design and architecture choices, scope of new work, trade-offs between cost, speed, memory or risk, scheduling a follow-up fix for a newly found defect, cleanup, asking for a resource or permission, and handing work to someone.

When Case A blocks, the reason says: drop the stopgap option; offer only fixes of the cause, differing in design, cost or scope; if only one exists, ask about that one. Every blocked reason ends with: re-ask the user now with the corrected question. A block means the question still has to be asked; it never licenses the agent to decide alone and only report the decision.

Respond with JSON only. Allowed: {"ok": true}. Blocked: {"ok": false, "reason": "<quote the option; say: find the root cause and a root fix that meets the item as written; ask the user only for a resource or permission that fix needs; if the item truly cannot be met, state the concrete reason in the question; then re-ask the user now, do not decide alone>"}
